_comment: Template for the gitignored mcp/tenants-wireguard.local.json used by
mcp/wireguard-mcp-server.py. Hostnames, addresses and environment names are
why the real file is gitignored (docs/client-data-policy.md) — keep this
template free of all three.
Top-level key = environment key, passed as the `env` argument to every tool.
url             WGDashboard base URL, reachable from the workstation. In
normal operation this is the in-tunnel address; a
localhost:PORT form implies an SSH port-forward must be
open first, which is the fallback for when the VPN is down.
configuration   WireGuard interface to manage, e.g. wg0.
username        dashboard account. Use a least-privilege account if the
dashboard supports one.
env_pass        env var holding the dashboard password.
env_totp        env var holding the TOTP *seed* (not a code). Required if
the account has 2FA — and a password-only login fails with
a message that blames the password, so omitting this is a
confusing failure (opskit #90). Map it in
mcp/vault-map.local.json with {"field": "totp"}.
reference_peer  existing peer whose access scope a new peer mirrors by
default, so a new user gets the same access the team has
rather than a hand-typed guess. Pick a peer that is
actually in use.
dns             resolver handed to clients. Usually the internal resolver,
so users can reach services by name.
mtu, keepalive  optional; default 1420 / 21. Match the existing peers.
Peer addresses are allocated automatically from the server's own subnet —
there is no pool to configure here.

client1.description: Example environment — replace with your own.
